name: Hip External Rotation
definition: A strict unilateral open-chain hip isolation performed supine on a treatment table with both hips flexed to 30 degrees over a wedge. A therapist stabilizes the working knee against the support and holds an elastic band attached at the working ankle while the lower leg moves through external hip rotation from neutral to the middle of the participant's available range. The pelvis and spine remain supported and do not create the repetition. The FOHX protocol directly reports this topology, approximately 10-to-12-repetition-maximum resistance, and three sets of ten; the completed trial supports only the whole multi-exercise hip program and does not isolate this record's outcome. Position-matched cadaveric torque evidence makes the obturator-internus/gemelli conjoined tendon primary and supports obturator externus and piriformis as mechanics-derived secondaries at 30 degrees. Quadratus femoris is also a mechanics-derived secondary: Delp supports its external-rotation direction, but Ito excluded it and therefore does not rank it against the three measured units. Obliques and medial hamstrings receive mechanics-derived stabilizer credit for the held spine, pelvis, and flexed knee under ankle-applied resistance; neither earns prime-action volume. All four mover regions are explicitly unvisualized because BodyModel.scn has no matching surfaces; no visible muscle receives proxy mover credit. Whole gluteus maximus, gluteus medius, and sartorius remain unassigned because capability does not establish exercise emphasis and their unsplit or multi-action anatomy does not justify a role here. Seated, side-lying, prone, clamshell, standing, cable, machine, self-anchored-band, combined-extension, and unassisted variants remain outside this contract.

exercises.name: Therapist-Held Supine Band Hip External Rotation
movementSteps: Lie on your back on a treatment table with both thighs supported over the wedge so your hips stay bent at 30 degrees and your knees stay bent.
Secure the elastic band at the working ankle.
Have the therapist hold the working knee against the support and pull the other end of the band against the movement.
Keep your pelvis and back still, and begin with the working thigh pointing straight ahead.
Move the working lower leg inward against the band until you reach the middle of your comfortable range.
Return to the straight-ahead position without lifting or turning the working thigh, and finish the set before changing sides.
